summary:
ASTRO PULSE is an offline Python dashboard that helps astronauts notice health changes against their own normal, not a population average. Every person has different physiology, so a general threshold can miss meaningful individual shifts or raise constant false alarms.

The system builds a personal baseline from the first ten days of a log, then converts each new day into z-scores. Nine measurements (sleep, resting heart rate, HRV, exercise, grip strength, stress, reaction-test lapses, body temperature and radiation dose) are grouped into the challenge’s four risk domains, each shown as a green, yellow or red status. A deviation must persist three consecutive days in the same direction before it raises an alert, and every alert explains in plain language what changed, by how much and for how long. A built-in reaction test, daily entry form, cumulative radiation tracking and an exportable report complete the workflow.

Because it runs without a server or connection to Earth, crews can assess themselves autonomously despite communication delays. In simulated tests with 100 astronauts, personal baselines produced fewer false alarms than a fixed threshold. ASTRO PULSE is a decision-support aid, not a diagnostic tool, and these results are synthetic.
details:
ASTRO PULSE is a software solution designed to support astronaut health monitoring during long-duration space missions. Its central idea is that every astronaut has different physiological and cognitive characteristics. Therefore, evaluating their health exclusively through general population standards may overlook meaningful individual changes.

Our system addresses this challenge through personalized health baselines. Before a mission, ASTRO PULSE analyzes an astronaut's historical measurements to establish their individual reference values. During the mission, it evaluates daily health records against these personal baselines, identifying deviations that could indicate emerging health concerns.

One of ASTRO PULSE's main advantages is its capacity for autonomous, offline analysis. Astronauts can upload daily measurement logs, including spreadsheet-based records, allowing the system to analyze collected information without requiring continuous communication with Earth. This reduces dependence on ground-based analysis and facilitates health monitoring during missions with communication delays or limited connectivity.

Furthermore, ASTRO PULSE aims to reduce the astronauts' daily workload by allowing existing measurements to be integrated into the system instead of relying exclusively on repetitive questionnaires. Objective measurements can also reveal discrepancies between an astronaut's self-reported well-being and their actual performance.

Our intended impact is to support astronauts' well-being, autonomy, and mission safety by identifying individual changes earlier and providing useful information for health-related decisions. The collected records could also contribute to post-mission medical evaluations by providing doctors with a longitudinal history of the astronaut's measurements.

By analyzing these records offline, it helps identify unusual changes without relying on constant communication with Earth. Its goal is to support astronauts' well-being and provide useful health data for medical evaluation, both during and after missions.
